headline_marked: [[Meta's Muse outpaces ChatGPT]] in early mobile downloads and daily active users
headline: Meta's Muse outpaces ChatGPT in early mobile downloads and daily active users
summary: New data from Apptopia indicates Meta's AI app, Muse, has surpassed ChatGPT in initial mobile downloads and daily active users in the U.S. and Canada iOS markets during its first 12 days.
details: Meta's new AI app, Muse, is showing stronger early mobile performance than ChatGPT, according to market intelligence firm Apptopia. In its first 12 days, Muse recorded 1.8 million iOS downloads in the U.S. and Canada, compared to ChatGPT's 1.3 million during its initial launch period.

This comparison specifically focuses on iOS data for the U.S. and Canada to ensure an apples-to-apples metric, as both apps had different global and platform launch strategies. Muse also demonstrated higher daily active users than ChatGPT at a similar point after its debut.

Globally, Muse has accumulated 2.8 million total installs within its first 12 days and has climbed to the No. 1 spot on the U.S. App Store. This rapid ascent suggests significant user adoption and engagement.

In the U.S. mobile app market, Muse currently boasts 642,000 daily active users, significantly higher than ChatGPT's 231,000 at the equivalent post-launch stage. Even when narrowed to iOS users only, Muse maintains a lead with 359,000 daily active users.

While Apptopia's figures are third-party estimates, they strongly indicate Muse's potential to become another major success for Meta. The company has a proven track record of leveraging its ecosystem for app growth, as seen with Threads.

Meta is expected to employ a similar cross-promotion strategy for Muse, integrating the AI app with its popular platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. This extensive network could provide a substantial boost to Muse's user base.

Apptopia's data supports this potential, showing that over 95% of Muse users are also Facebook users, and 63% are Instagram users. This existing user overlap makes cross-platform promotion highly effective.

headline_marked: [[Ukrainian naval drone sinks Russian kamikaze drone boat]] in world's first USV-on-USV combat
headline: Ukrainian naval drone sinks Russian kamikaze drone boat in world's first USV-on-USV combat
summary: In a historic first, a Ukrainian Sargan-3000 naval drone used a remote machine gun to destroy a Russian Orcan explosive drone boat in the Black Sea. The engagement marks a new era in naval warfare.
details: The world's first confirmed drone boat vs. drone boat combat occurred on September 12, as a Ukrainian naval drone destroyed a Russian explosive drone boat. The Ukrainian vessel used a remote-controlled machine gun turret to neutralize its target.

Ukraine's Defense Intelligence detected the Russian uncrewed surface vessel (USV), identified as an Orcan surface drone. These "jet ski type" vessels are designed to ram targets and explode, and have previously attacked Ukrainian ports and ships.

The Ukrainian Sargan-3000 drone boat was armed with a 12.7 mm machine gun mounted on a remote weapon station from Norwegian company Kongsberg. It engaged the Russian drone from a distance of one kilometer.

Video released by the Ukrainian Navy shows the Sargan-3000 disabling the Russian drone's communications antenna before riddling it with bullets until it sank. The Sargan-3000 can reach speeds of 40-55 knots and travel up to 1,600 kilometers.

Ukraine has heavily invested in developing and deploying drone boats for asymmetric warfare against Russia's Black Sea Fleet. These efforts have reportedly sunk Russian ships and targeted oil/gas transport vessels.

Naval drone innovations extend beyond combat, with Ukraine using USVs to deploy ground robots and as motherships for FPV drones. This evolving drone warfare highlights a growing global threat, as Russia also deploys similar naval drones.

The US military has also used drone boats in combat, attacking an Iranian port facility and rescuing pilots. This underscores the increasing role of uncrewed surface vessels in modern military operations worldwide.
